Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

litterfitter 0.2.0 (GitHub only; not released to CRAN)

Behaviour changes

  • fit_litter() now defaults to model = "neg.exp" when no model is given.
  • fit_litter() warns when mass remaining values are above 1 or below 0 (see Bug fixes).
  • Fits can differ slightly from earlier versions because of the smaller optimiser step.
  • steady_state() returns Inf for neg.exp.limit fits with B > 0 (previously a string).
  • time_to_prop_mass_remaining() returns NA (with a warning) when the threshold is never reached, and its result is now exact rather than read off a grid, so values may differ slightly.
  • coef() now returns a named vector.

Bug fixes

  • fit_litter() now defaults to model = "neg.exp" and rejects unknown model names (previously omitting model gave “first argument has length > 1”).
  • Proportional mass remaining values above 1 (apparent mass gain from measurement error, common early in decomposition or when decomposition is slow) are kept in the fit but now trigger an informative warning of class litterfitter_mass_above_one; when the data also show little overall mass loss the warning says that parameters may be poorly constrained and derived quantities are extrapolations (#21). Slightly negative values (down to -0.1) are kept with a litterfitter_mass_below_zero warning; clearly negative values or percentages are errors.
  • fit_litter() now rejects infinite values, invalid iters, and data with a single time point; drops missing observations with a warning; and requires more observations than parameters.
  • Boundary warnings now name the parameters on a bound, and hint that the default bounds assume time in years when time values are large.
  • Litter fits and their bootstrap replicates use analytic gradients for all six curves (#27), improving accuracy for small rates such as rates per day. discrete.series now supports equal pool rates. Element fits and calls with gr = NULL use finite differences (default ndeps = 1e-4). Built-in gradients use a default limit of 500 optimizer iterations so that cont.quality fits can converge along a shallow minimum. An explicit control$maxit takes precedence. In a local benchmark on pineneedles (median of three fixed-seed runs), the 200-start discrete.series fit took 0.078 s versus 0.109 s previously, and 200 bootstrap replicates took 0.053 s versus 0.080 s.
  • Weibull fits and bootstraps require a strictly positive lower bound for the scale parameter beta. Bootstrap replicates that reach the optimizer’s iteration limit or otherwise fail to converge are recorded as NA.
  • The “may not have found global best fit” check now compares the 5 best fits (it previously compared the 5 worst) and no longer errors when fewer than 5 starts succeed.
  • steady_state() for neg.exp.limit now returns a number (Inf when B > 1e-4, otherwise A / k) instead of a string, fixing errors in summary() and bootstrap_parameters().
  • bootstrap_parameters() records failed replicates as NA instead of erroring.
  • time_to_prop_mass_remaining() now uses uniroot(): exact, fast, independent of time units, and returns NA with a warning when the threshold is never reached.
  • Plot curves use a fixed number of points regardless of time units; plot_multiple_fits() no longer clips mass values above 1.
  • Fixed Weibull and discrete.series formula display in plot.litfit().
  • plot.litfit() always shows the (0, 1) starting point on the y axis (#7).
  • All six models are now documented in ?fit_litter; neg.exp had been accidentally commented out and neg.exp.limit was missing (#22).
  • time_to_prop_mass_remaining() gives a clear error for a missing threshold.mass.
  • Restored input-validation tests that were lost in 0.1.5, and greatly expanded the test suite (edge cases for inputs, every model, derived quantities checked against closed-form results, bootstrap failures, methods and plots).

New features

  • New methods (#19): print.litfit(), logLik.litfit() (so AIC(fit1, fit2) and BIC() work), nobs.litfit(), residuals.litfit() and summary.litfit_bootstrap().
  • coef() and bootstrap output now carry parameter names.
  • New quiet argument to fit_litter() suppresses the “successful fits” message.
  • plot_multiple_fits() invisibly returns the fitted models.

Performance and dependencies

  • Model fitting is roughly 3-4x faster (objective function built once per fit).
  • Dropped the methods dependency; removed unused devtools/roxygen2 from Suggests.

litterfitter 0.1.5

  • fixing url in the readme, which is causing a note in the cran checks
  • Modernized package structure and code style (styler, lintr)
  • Updated GitHub Actions workflows for better CI/CD support (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows)
  • Updated dependencies (R >= 4.1.0)

litterfitter 0.1.4

CRAN release: 2025-08-21

  • removed plyr dependency for long term ease of maintanance
  • updated testing framework to testthat v3 style
  • fixed a testing instability that was causing occasional warnings
  • updating doi syntax

litterfitter 0.1.3

CRAN release: 2023-08-29

  • updated package level documentation
  • improved documentation for a number of functions
  • moving github home to traitecoevo

litterfitter 0.1.2

CRAN release: 2022-09-15

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.
